question: Assume today is 2026-10-19. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate total milk production in the 24 major States of the United States in September 2026, in pounds (the report states it in million pounds), as it will be first reported in the USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service's monthly Milk Production report.

target.what: Total milk production in the 24 major milk-producing States of the United States during September 2026, as first published by USDA NASS in the monthly Milk Production report (million pounds, converted here to pounds)
target.caveats: Target period is completed (Sept 2026) but the first report covering it would be released around late October 2026, after the 2026-10-19 cutoff, so no published value exists at cutoff. Working interpretation: the '24 major States' aggregate as NASS defines it (the 24 top milk-producing States, which

candidates.perspective: NASS monthly Milk Production report time series
candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 24-State production ≈ September 2025 value adjusted for the recent year-over-year growth trend and any month-specific deviation; September is typically a seasonal low-to-mid month. The prior-year same-month value plus trend growth is the primary anchor.
candidates.data_to_find: NASS 24-State monthly milk production (million lb) for September 2025 and for all months Jan 2025–Aug 2026 (or latest available before cutoff), plus the year-over-year percent change in recent months. Minimum: Sept 2025 value and the most recent 3-6 months of 24-State totals.

candidates.perspective: USDA milk production forecasts and dairy market reports
candidates.hypothesis: USDA WASDE and ERS forecasts give annual/quarterly US milk production; the 24-State share of US total is stable (~85-90%), so US total × share gives an independent cross-check on the 24-State September figure.
candidates.data_to_find: USDA WASDE or ERS milk supply forecasts for 2026 (annual and quarterly US milk production, billion lb), and the historical ratio of 24-State to all-US monthly production. Minimum: 2026 annual US production forecast and the 24-State share.

candidates.hypothesis: 24-State production = (24-State milk cow inventory) × (milk produced per cow per month). Both are reported in the same NASS report; using recent cow numbers and per-cow yields gives a bottom-up estimate for September 2026.
candidates.data_to_find: NASS 24-State milk cow inventory (thousand head) and milk per cow (lb/month) for recent months (mid-2026) and September 2025; recent trends in both. Minimum: latest cow inventory and per-cow yield, plus Sept 2025 same.

candidates.data_to_find: Reports of dairy herd disease outbreaks, heat waves in major dairy states (CA, WI, ID, TX, NY) in summer 2026, feed price shocks, or farm closures affecting Sept 2026 output. Minimum: any documented event with quantified herd or yield impact.

assumptions.name: August-to-September 24-State production ratio
assumptions.rationale: September is a seasonal low-to-mid month relative to August. In 2025 the 24-State total fell from 18.8 billion lb (Aug) to 18.3 billion lb (Sep), a ratio of ~0.973; the range reflects year-to-year variation in the seasonal decline.
assumptions.applies_when: Applying the observed August 2026 24-State level forward to September 2026, assuming a normal seasonal decline similar to 2025.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 production held flat or rose versus August 2026, or a materially different Aug-Sep seasonal pattern.

assumptions.name: September 2026 YoY growth factor for 24-State production
assumptions.rationale: Recent 24-State YoY growth was 1.8% in July and August 2026 (p25, p7), with US growth ~1.7%; the LMIC Q3 forecast of +0.9% suggests possible slowing, so the range spans 0% to +4%.
assumptions.applies_when: Applying the September 2025 24-State level forward one year using the recent growth trend.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp acceleration or contraction in September 2026 24-State production growth.

assumptions.name: September 2026 24-State milk per cow relative to August 2026
assumptions.rationale: Per-cow yield declines seasonally from August to September; in 2025 it fell from 2,066 lb (Aug) to 1,999 lb (Sep), a ratio of ~0.968. Range reflects seasonal variability.
assumptions.applies_when: Bottom-up cow x yield route using August 2026 per-cow yield projected to September.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 per-cow yield was near or above the August level.

assumptions.name: August-to-September 24-State production ratio
assumptions.rationale: September is a seasonal low-to-mid month. Using NASS 24-State levels: Sep 2025 18,230 / Aug 2025 18,827 = 0.968; Sep 2024 17,500 / Aug 2024 18,200 = 0.962. Both years give ~0.96-0.97; center at 0.973 with a range spanning 0.955-0.99 to allow for year-to-year seasonal variation.
assumptions.applies_when: The Aug 2026 level (p6) is a valid base and the Aug-to-Sep seasonal ratio is stable across years.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 had an unusual heat event or herd loss that broke the normal seasonal decline.

assumptions.name: September 2026 YoY growth factor for 24-State production
assumptions.rationale: Recent 24-State YoY growth: Aug 2026 +1.8% (p7), July 2026 +1.8% (p25), Feb 2026 +3.1% (p21), Jan 2026 +3.6% (p54). Growth has decelerated toward ~1.8%; LMIC Q3 forecast +0.9% (p55) is a downside. Center at 1.018 with range 1.00-1.04.
assumptions.applies_when: September 2026 YoY growth is close to the recent August/July 1.8% trend.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp September slowdown (e.g., H5N1 herd losses, heat) or a reacceleration above 4%.

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: Most direct route: apply the historical Aug-to-Sep seasonal ratio to the observed Aug 2026 24-State level. Shared dependency: p6 is a preliminary NASS figure subject to revision (~0.5% typical). Failure mode: an unusual September 2026 shock (heat, H5N1) that breaks the seasonal pattern.

methods.label: m2

a2.role: September 2026 YoY growth factor for 24-State production

methods.rationale: YoY trend route: apply the recent 24-State YoY growth factor to the Sep 2025 level. Growth factor is anchored on Aug/Jul 2026 +1.8% actuals (p7, p25) with a downside allowance for the stale LMIC +0.9% forecast (p55). Shared dependency: p1 is a revised NASS figure; a2 is an assumption. Failure mode: a September-specific growth deviation.

methods.label: m3

p12.role: 24-State average milk per cow, August 2026 (pounds per cow per month)

a3.role: September 2026 24-State milk per cow relative to August 2026

methods.rationale: Bottom-up route: Aug 2026 cows x Aug 2026 per-cow x Aug-to-Sep per-cow seasonal ratio. Uses the same NASS August release as m1 (shared dependency on p10/p12), so it is not fully independent of m1, but it decomposes the level differently and tests whether the cow x yield identity holds. Failure mode: September cow inventory differs from August (herd growth ~15,000/month) and per-cow seasonal ratio

kept.name: August-to-September 24-State production ratio
kept.rationale: September is a seasonal low-to-mid month. Using NASS 24-State levels: Sep 2025 18,230 / Aug 2025 18,827 = 0.968; Sep 2024 17,500 / Aug 2024 18,200 = 0.962. Both years give ~0.96-0.97; center at 0.973 with a range spanning 0.955-0.99 to allow for year-to-year seasonal variation.
kept.applies_when: The Aug 2026 level (p6) is a valid base and the Aug-to-Sep seasonal ratio is stable across years.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that September 2026 had an unusual heat event or herd loss that broke the normal seasonal decline.

kept.name: September 2026 YoY growth factor for 24-State production
kept.rationale: Recent 24-State YoY growth: Aug 2026 +1.8% (p7), July 2026 +1.8% (p25), Feb 2026 +3.1% (p21), Jan 2026 +3.6% (p54). Growth has decelerated toward ~1.8%; LMIC Q3 forecast +0.9% (p55) is a downside. Center at 1.018 with range 1.00-1.04.
kept.applies_when: September 2026 YoY growth is close to the recent August/July 1.8% trend.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of a sharp September slowdown (e.g., H5N1 herd losses, heat) or a reacceleration above 4%.

kept.name: September 2026 24-State milk per cow relative to August 2026
kept.applies_when: The Aug 2026 per-cow (p12) is a valid base and the Aug-to-Sep per-cow ratio is stable.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of an unusual September 2026 yield shock (heat, disease) that breaks the normal seasonal decline.

residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
